verdict: Rollout FAILED: the experiment ran, but val_bpb = 1.015072 did not improve on the current best 1.013025 by more than the required 0.0005 (lower is better).

insights_in_context.hint: Reducing MLP capacity to buy more steps made the model under-capacity, so the experiment should not have shrunk the 4x MLP expansion.
The bad choice was treating extra value-embedding tables as free capacity when they actually cost steps and undertrained within the fixed time budget.

Don't buy steps by cutting model capacity the way batch-halving did — GQA removed ~21% of params for only a ~4% speedup, so pick a capacity-neutral speedup or a small capacity/optimizer change instead.

insight.hint: Depth 10 at width 512 costs too many optimizer steps for this 5-minute budget, so stop pushing depth and try an optimizer or efficiency-neutral change instead.

judge.summary: The agent inspected train.py and results.tsv, then chose to continue the recently successful depth-increase line by changing DEPTH from 9 to 10 while keeping MODEL_DIM = 512 and max-autotune unchanged. It committed the one-line edit, ran the experiment, and obtained val_bpb 1.015072 with 27.7 GB peak memory, which is worse than the current best 1.013025 and therefore does not meet the improvement threshold.
judge.feedback: The implementation and run were clean; the failure was in the experimental choice, specifically the decision in the edit step to increase DEPTH to 10. The 8 -> 9 depth improvement did not imply that further depth was still beneficial at this compute budget: the depth-10 run used more parameters (60.8M vs 57.7M) and produced fewer optimizer steps (1681 vs 1844), leading to a clear regression of about 0.002. The reasoning over-extrapolated the previous depth win and under-weighted the step-count cost of adding another layer at fixed width. The first substantive error was therefore the choice to test DEPTH = 10 as a promising next capacity increment rather than a more likely efficiency-neutral or optimizer-side tweak.
